description:
The Grammo table lamp uses weighted glass spheres placed onto an elastic membrane surface to physically control light activation and diffusion. When a frosted sphere is set on the flexible top fabric, its weight deforms the tensioned surface downward, activating an ambient glow from the internal LED module beneath.

Instead of relying on digital switches or touch-sensitive electronics, the fixture operates through direct mechanical displacement. As the weight depresses the flexible textile cover closer to the light source inside the clear cylindrical body, the downward pressure changes the distance and angle of the shade. Using spheres of different sizes alters the depth of the membrane stretch, creating distinct light levels and shadows.

Designed by Habits Design for Italian manufacturer Martinelli Luce, the lamp reimagines modern lighting control as an interactive kinetic sculpture. By utilizing gravity and physical weight as an analog dimmer interface, the system provides an intuitive visual and tactile connection between mass and light intensity.
